pageCache.text:
Why Carden?
Together we aspire, learn, achieve and thrive.
Watch Carden in action
Our pupils are absolutely at the heart of every decision we make and as a staff team we are dedicated and care passionately about what we do.
We pride ourselves on the outstanding level of care shown for each individual child: from a personal welcome at the school gate to lessons designed with each child in mind. We know which pupil is obsessed with mini-beasts; who has had a big change in their lives; or who is a budding inventor. We work hard to ensure that every child is – and feels – safe, and has a caring and supportive environment in which to work, grow and enjoy time.
Our goal is to work with parents and carers to prepare pupils not only for their next stage of education academically, but also with life skills and a good level of emotional resilience.
Tour Reception area online
In Reception at Carden we believe in giving children lots of rich, exciting, wide-ranging experiences which help them develop secure and positive friendships, builds their confidence and gives them a secure foundation to base all their future learning upon.
Carden school grounds
The building is spacious, with large windows letting in lots of light and air. There are doors from each classroom onto patio areas, and playing fields. This means the children have ample space to learn and play.
Yet large classrooms and grounds doesn’t mean it’s an overwhelming space for younger pupils. Carden has created three connected but separate areas for different age groups.
Latest update
This week we went to visit the new housing development at the old Hollingbury Library site. The children got a chance to look around the flats. We spotted our school and looked for local sites from the roof gardens. The building is ecological and we learnt about the solar panels and the heating system. The developers also talked to the children all about how the flats have been designed and built and what jobs were needed to create them. Perhaps some future careers for our children in there.... ... Parent/carer & pupil feedback
My son is now in yr4 and is excelling. I have a young son too also in carden and his reading, writing, and general life knowledge in the last year has blown me away, and that’s all down to the teachers and staff at carden.
Over the years we’ve had the added benefit of the swimming pool opening for KS1 children and this year we have also got the added bonus of our outdoor learning program coming together, utilising the fab amount of outdoor space carden has.
Current Yr 4 and Yr 1 parent
We chose Carden The diversity was a big factor for me I wanted my kids to be able to relate to and be friends with who are different from them(carden is something like 45% BAME).
The large amount of outdoor space was also an appeal as was the fact is a primary school rather than two separate schools. I’m glad my boy who is now in year two doesn’t have to change schools at the end of the year. I also seem to relate more to Carden‘s headteacher. I have been very happy with my choice both of my boys have thrived at Carden.
We love Carden - I have two there and one who will go in a couple of years. It’s a real community school where being part of the school extends outside of school hours.
What I love (and didn’t realise quite how important it would be to my shame), is because the school has such a great mix of people, there are no outsiders there. Everyone (and every child) is treated as the unique individual they are and it makes a really wonderful melting pot.

It felt like a warm atmosphere when we went around. I found the head really inspiring and liked her vision for the school. I also feel the outdoor space and pe teaching were a draw. Finally I felt they would support my child better if he developed any difficulties with learning (which he hasn't so far).
My daughter goes to Carden and it’s fantastic she is so happy there. Really lovely community spirit and the Headteacher is amazing. It’s really diverse and inclusive and that’s part of the reason I love it so much. It’s really warm and welcoming and all of the teachers and staff are so lovely!! The fact they have a swimming pool with weekly swimming lessons is definitely an added bonus!
I can safely say from my Children’s experience Carden has been an absolutely wonderful place for them. It’s diverse, inclusive, warm, creative and the staff care deeply about the children. During lock down they were so creative with what they offered.
My son has blossomed in reception, he has forest school, a designated art teacher and sports teacher and next year will be able to use the swimming pool. My daughter in year 6 has loved every moment and will be so sad to leave next year.
Current Yr 6 and Reception Parent
My daughter has actually left Carden now but when she was there the school was amazing with her and can’t fault it at all.
Carden has a beautiful scheme of getting the Year 6 children to buddy up with a Reception child and the benefit for both is incredible.
Every classroom opens up onto a playground, there is a pond, an orchard, a running track, a swimming pool and a wood all in the school grounds. Plus if you have to drop your child off, there is plenty of easy parking around the school.
I feel quite jealous of parents about to become part of Carden because my youngest daughter is in year 4 so I only have 2&1/2 years left of the loveliness of it all!
Educationally Carden is excellent, my older daughter just started at Patcham High and it was such an easy transition, She is thriving as she did at Carden. She loves traditional classroom learning and Carden gave her that and so much more.
I chose Carden because it is diverse and inclusive and that has been even more beneficial than I realised it would be.
Former parent and current Yr 4 parent
It is a huge school, that is really small! The children benefit from the masses of space, but small year groups and class numbers mean the children get a lot of attention and development opportunities. As a site, it's not 'over-developed'.
I picked a school for my first child and didn't even think about my second. Ofsted recently (2021) recognised Carden as good at Maths, English, Art, Science, French, PE... the list goes on, so both of my very different children are doing exceptionally well. Also, they are great with winter and summer borns, they just get them!
I (and my kids) have become friends with so many people from all walks of life and it’s lovely. It’s a real egalitarian hub. (Plus there’s all the wonderful sporting facilities, outdoor learning and forest school, specialist art and PE lessons, camping trips on the school field, fab PTA organised events etc).
The building is not traditionally pretty but actually inside you see the benefit of the layout with the huge windows making it so light and airy, and the doors on each classroom leading outside so lessons can move outside whenever necessary.
Carden is a community of parents, children and teachers; during lockdown we all supported each other. There is always so much going on through the PTA as well that only adds to the school experience such as discos, fireworks, film night, bake offs, fetes, trails, pamper evenings, a colour run and new events all the time!
Diversity is a word that is used a lot, but what does it actually mean? Carden is a mix of ethnicities, religions, educational needs and class, and my children are far better human beings for it and they are being set up for an amazing future.
The things that was important to us was that we can walk to school, be close to school friends. My son was using hearing aids at the time, so noise was a factor too. I found Carden really lovely, the inside is so amazing, it was just a better fit for him. Carden has been really good supporting him with his needs.
It’s an amazing school. My daughter is Autistic and their Senco is just beyond supportive and actually listens. All the staff I have also found to be so lovely.
The outside space the school has is amazing and they have recently opened up their own swimming pool which my daughter loves.
Carden is such a a warm and inclusive school. I highly recommend.
Carden is really truly a special school. The warmth and inclusiveness is above and beyond. It really does feel like a family rather than a school and so does the lovely community. I feel so lucky through the PTA I’ve met so many other local families that have really supported each other in these weird last few years.

When visiting carden for the first time with my son, I was greeted by a lovey kind lady who had already took it upon herself to know my sons name and greet him and myself at the door. On walking around I knew very quickly that carden was the school I wanted my son to be in. It not only has the excellent PE provisions, outstanding phonics and reading results, but it also has the love, the care, the nurturing, the fun and the most beautiful community supporting it.
Carden will forever have my heart!

It’s an amazing school, amazingly supportive community, teachers & staff are so kind & caring & the SEN team if ever you should need it as we have found we do for emotional reasons are second to none.
Yes it’s a bigger school but the Nursery & Reception are quite separate so that it eases children in more quietly although they do go to the bigger playground as a class & use the sports hall etc & year 1 is also fenced off to give them that bit of security. They have so much space, sports dept have awards & my children are doing well & are really happy there.

Modern Foreign Languages
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities in different languages. Our aim is to engage and instil pupils with a love of learning and appreciation of other languages enabling them to be successful, confident multi-lingual citizens of the future. Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our language rich curriculum which is mapped to include coverage of the national curriculum as well as numerous enrichment activities within school and use of opportunities within our wider community.
Our languages curriculum, that follows the scheme iLanguages, motivates pupils to be passionate risk takers when speaking other languages both in and out of school. We want to encourage a sense of curiosity to enable pupils to make links between languages; to understand shared history and to use knowledge of other languages to enhance English skills and vocabulary. We believe that the languages curriculum should be embedded throughout the day, both in and out of the classroom. We value, respect and celebrate the diverse range of languages spoken within our community. Our ultimate goal is for our learners to have a global positive mind-set towards all languages that will facilitate opportunities for now and in the future.
Implementation
At Carden, we use a high-quality foreign languages scheme of work, iLanguages to teach French. Embedded in the scheme are the skills progression of all the key skills of listening, speaking, reading, writing and grammar through well-planned lessons that that include games, songs, interactive activities and stories. The children’s skills are developed through weekly teaching in KS2 with accompanying audio from a native speaker to support with pronunciation. Children build on previous knowledge gradually as their foreign language lessons continue to recycle, revise and consolidate previously learnt language.
All of the lessons have clearly defined objectives and aims, they incorporate interactive activities to allow for speaking and listening, have challenge sections to stretch their learning, as well as independent activities for reading and writing of various difficulty to support each child’s learning needs.
The lessons are underpinned by our school’s Learning Journey Skills and Core Values, giving children opportunities to be creative, kind, take risks, show independence, curiosity and perseverance in their learning. The history and evolution of French and English are studied and links between the two languages are drawn upon across the whole curriculum and in assemblies to support pupils with seeing connections, consolidating knowledge and improving vocabulary choices.
In addition to learning French, over 20 languages are spoken within the Carden community. We encourage children to share key words and phrases with each other and adults in order to celebrate our rich and diverse community.
Impact
The outcome of teaching French as a foreign language is that pupils increase their level of challenge, stretch and linguistic and grammatical complexity, moving from introductory units through to intermediate units and into the most challenging progressive units in Y6. This will enable them to feel more confident in speaking, reading and writing in French. By developing these skills, pupils will be able to use and apply their learning in a variety of contexts, laying down solid foundations for future language learning. Pupils will continuously build on their cognitive ability, using their previous knowledge as they progress in their foreign language learning journey. Overtime their confidence, fluency and enthusiasm for French and the learning of languages will grow, allowing them to use their skills to communicate with people from all around the world, to travel around the world and to feel confident and work in settings where their language skills are an asset.

Implementation & impact
Curriculum rationale
Carden's Core Values
Our core values underpin our curriculum and link to rewards and celebrations. One child described our core values as like the “writing that goes through a stick of rock”. We expect all our children and staff to adhere to these values alongside British Values at all times.
Implementation & impact
Curriculum Implementation and Impact
At Carden, our curriculum, schemes of work and individual lessons are sequenced and planned effectively. The curriculum is robust, ambitious, and ensures plentiful examples of enrichment opportunities including trips, visitors and themed days. Eight concepts run through all areas of the curriculum: language rich, imagination, celebration, curiosity, valuing equality, being active, purposeful and outdoor learning – see separate subject pages for more detail.
We use the National Curriculum (for Year 1 to 6) and Development Matters (for EYFS) to provide the content and framework for what we teach to ensure that coverage is broad and balanced and that key knowledge is securely understood. This enables our children to make links across their learning as they progress through the school. This starts from the time our children join us, ensuring that learning is a cohesive journey from Early Years through to Year 6.
We focus on the quality of our teaching, positive relationships between children and adults and between children and their peers as well as embedding high expectations, to ensure that our children receive a broad and balanced curriculum. This allows them to develop resilience, ambition and a confidence in themselves that will remain with them for many years to come. Our curriculum is ambitious for all pupils. In every subject, teachers expertly identify any barriers to learning for pupils and overcome these. Our expectation is that teachers will adapt the curriculum to meet the needs of all learners ensuring challenge and scaffolded support for learning wherever necessary.
Our early year’s curriculum is carefully constructed and highly effective in developing the youngest children’s learning and personal development. The curriculum introduces children in Nursery and Reception Years to key English and mathematics vocabulary and early concepts, which supports them for future learning. Teaching of phonics across the school is robust. We are fortunate enough to have longstanding experienced EYFS practitioners who work full time with our reception classes.
Our curriculum is underpinned by our 5 core values of Respect, Kindness, Safety, Aspiration and Courage and 13 learning journey skills that are introduced in EYFS and developed throughout the school represented by animals such as the cat (encourage questions) the bee (work together and independently) and the unicorn (to be imaginative). These are threaded through all learning and form part of our teaching/learning and behaviour policy. We want our pupils to leave Carden with these core value and skills embedded in order to prepare them for the next stage of their learning.
Learning outside is a priority for us. We have amazing school grounds that are used all year round regardless of the weather. Each classroom has direct access to outdoor space where learning takes place daily. Our Outdoor Learning classroom is timetabled and used for curriculum work, team building activities, whole class rewards and gardening club. Our fields, ponds and environmental rainscape area provide us with lots of unique cross-curricular learning opportunities.
We are a Gold Mark Sports provision school and one of only five schools in the city with Farm School status, twinned with Balmer Farm for various activities throughout the year for different year groups. Our KS2 classes all work with IntoUni, an organisation to help young people aspire to be the best versions of themselves.
Pupils’ personal development is a particular strength of our curriculum as identified by OFSTED. Our commitment to equality and diversity lies at the heart of all we do and underpins pupils’ learning. Our curriculum is extremely diversified in terms of ethnicity, gender, sexuality, religion and reflect our diverse demographic. A third or our pupils are non-white British. All children can see people like themselves represented throughout all subjects at different times of the year. Our approach to Black History was used as an exemplar across other Brighton and Hove schools. We encourage pupils and their families to engage with each other in school events throughout the year such as our Eid family picnic, fireworks night, Diwali celebrations and various PTA events.
Our curriculum meets the specific needs of our children, taking into account their life experiences, backgrounds and varied starting points. We intentionally plan learning activities which build up pupils’ cultural capital by providing a rich range of experiences, texts, vocabulary, knowledge and skills. We develop the vocabulary of our pupils, teaching them previously unknown vocabulary, key words and language structures that they can then apply across the curriculum. We also provide a range of extra-curricular activities that enable our children to learn in different situations and beyond the curriculum subjects. Last academic year, 35 clubs were offered (22 sports and 13 non-sports) which included dance, Lego, board games, football, coding, gardening, golf, skateboarding and music. We encourage all pupils to take part in at least one enrichment activity.
Our Activity Passports encourage pupils to take part in many exciting and interesting activities both in an out of school. A list of twenty activities (6 completed as home learning tasks) develop a curiosity about the world. We our want pupils to be imaginative, motivated and to enjoy being outdoors. We want them to be confident, happy and successful learners.
All aspects of our curriculum help pupils become citizens of the future. We want our young people to make positive contributions to their community upholding British and Carden Core Values during their time with us and in the next stage of their learning and into adulthood. Many of our pupils choose to stay in touch when they leave updating us on their exciting experiences at university, global travel adventures and successful careers in a multitude of different workplaces.
Carden Learning Journey
Our learning journey consists of a set of skills that we want all children to be able to develop in order to be successful learners for each stage of their learning and for when they leave us. The skills are hooked to an animal which helps to the younger children to remember the skills needed to learn, achieve and thrive.
Curriculum rationale
Carden Curriculum Rationale
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities. Our aim is to engage and equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding they require to be successful learners.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our language rich curriculum which is mapped to include coverage of the national curriculum as well as numerous enrichment activities and outdoor learning opportunities. Our curriculum challenges all pupils; engages their imagination; encourages their curiosity and motivates them to take the next steps in their learning.
We believe that the curriculum is everything that happens throughout the day, both in and out of school; we value and celebrate experiences and achievements from home.
Our ultimate goal is for all learners to be successful, confident, happy individuals, who make positive contributions within their community, respect diversity and value equality of opportunity both now and in the future.

Religious Education
Intent
At Carden Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities. Our aim is to engage and equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding they require to be successful learners.
Through our teaching of R.E we aim to ensure that our children have an understanding and respect of the wider world and the rich diversity around us. By encouraging the children to discuss, explore and share different beliefs we foster a culture of inclusion and acceptance.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our language rich curriculum which is mapped to include coverage of the national curriculum as well as numerous enrichment activities and outdoor learning opportunities.
Our RE curriculum follows the Jigsaw scheme and is challenging, engaging and encourages a curiosity to question and learn from others. This is achieved through creative, active and purposeful experiences to fully engage the children.
We believe that the RE curriculum influences children’s understanding of others both in and out of school; we value and celebrate experiences and achievements from home and encourage the children to talk, discuss and accept our differences.
Our ultimate goal is for all learners to be confident, happy individuals, who make positive contributions within their community. We want our children to be curious about different religions and to accept and respect religious beliefs regardless of their own beliefs and practices.
Implementation
At Carden, we use the Jigsaw scheme of work to teach Religious Education. This is a comprehensive, enquiry-based RE curriculum for UK primary schools (ages 3-11/12) that teaches about major world religions and Humanism through flexible, well-resourced weekly lessons, focusing on big questions, personal reflection, and developing empathy, respect, and understanding of diverse worldviews. It’s designed to support the statutory RE curriculum, align with local agreed syllabi, and integrate personal, spiritual, moral, and cultural (SMSC) development.
Children start exploring Religious Education in the Early Years through learning about celebrations and festivals. Some religious themes are linked to our PSHE curriculum, understanding the world, expressive arts and design, literacy and maths.
The knowledge which children gain in the Early Years, supplements the KS1 curriculum planning, where children have an opportunity to further understand concepts in Christianity and Judaism. The curriculum is delivered through implementation of children’s previous knowledge in the next year group. Concepts, themes and ideas are extended and other religions such as Islam, Buddhism and Sikhism are studied as pupils move through KS2. In each year group children are given opportunities to build upon their knowledge and skills drawing upon real life experiences and current world issues and contexts.
Children make good links to learning when experiences of RE curriculum are made meaningful. For example, the school holds special religious and charitable events and assemblies to promote the key themes of religious education such as our Eid Family picnic, Diwali, Chinese New Year, Easter and Christmas celebrations. Members of the school community are invited to talk to children about their religions. Pupils have opportunities to visit local religious buildings.
Impact
Our RE curriculum and delivery helps children gain a love for learning and respect for different religions. Children show increasing knowledge about diverse communities and ways of life in each key stage. An effective programme of study helps children to gain skills necessary to hold balanced conversations about religions and worldviews. Teachers aim high to give educational opportunities which bring a positive outlook towards communities across the city and beyond. Overall, children are able to link their learning at school our Carden Core Values and British Values.

Music
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities. Our aim for music is for children to develop an understanding of the importance of music as a form of expression and promote its value. From sound discrimination in the EYFS up to performances in Year 6, we believe music can support and enhance the development of a multitude of skills and knowledge.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our teaching and promotion of music which strives to ensure equal opportunities for all children through experiences and active learning. When provided with the experience of various styles and instruments, including the voice, we believe children will become successful learners in this subject.
Our music curriculum challenges all pupils; engages their imagination through experiences and composition; encourages their curiosity within and across a variety of musical styles, and may motivate them to become more specified musicians with individual tuition, through our close link with the organisation Rocksteady.
We believe that the curriculum is everything that happens throughout the day, both in and out of school; we value and celebrate the sharing of musical experiences and performances, both by pupils and professionals.
Our ultimate goal is to ignite a passion and appreciation of music in all learners and in doing so widen their world view of the importance of music within communities, across barriers and in their future lives.
Implementation
Carden has tried and tested various schemes of work for music such as Charanga and Sing Up however the decision to move away from a scheme has enabled the curriculum to become more bespoke the community. Cross curricular links are made and the skills and characters of the Learning Journey are heavily embedded. Musical theatre forms and important element for each year group and draws upon the skills and expertise of Brighton and Hove Operative Society who are resident on site.
The music and curriculum lead have created a scheme of work that covers the expectations of the national curriculum and is supported by a progression of skills document. Pupils are encouraged to study different musicians through the ages; practise their own skills in singing and playing instruments; evaluating their own and other pupils’ performances and produce end of unit pieces both collaboratively and on their own.
During music lessons, the children have the opportunity to explore a diverse array of musical instruments, allowing them to discover the rhythm within songs and play along. This hands-on approach also encourages the exploration of improvisation and composition, complementing the music being studied in class.
A weekly key stage singing assembly is an integral part of the curriculum, where songs often have connections to the PSHE (Personal, Social, Health, and Economic) curriculum, placing singing at the core of promoting well-being among the pupils. Singing has proven to enhance self-esteem, boost confidence, improve self-efficacy, offer an outlet for emotions, and support interpersonal communication.
Performance holds a central place in Carden’s musical teaching and learning philosophy. All pupils actively participate in key stage performances during Christmas shows; year group assemblies and the theatre productions. These performances are open to parents, who are warmly invited to attend and appreciate their children’s musical talents.
Carden partners with the organisation Rocksteady who deliver inclusive band lessons designed to amplify children’s self-belief, support wellbeing and help maximise their potential back in the classroom. These sessions are open to every child across the school.
Peripatetic teachers offer bespoke music lessons for children interested in playing keyboards, guitar and violin encouraging students to explore and develop their musical interests and talents.

Computing
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities. Our aim is to ensure all children are digitally literate – able to use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through, information and communication technology. Equipping them with a variety of skills (computational thinking, creativity and problem solving) prepares them for the future workplace and enables them to be active participants in a digital world.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin the teaching of computing. Our computing curriculum from Purple Mash, challenges all children. Through the programme of study, children learn the fundamental principles and processes of computation; they gain repeated, practical experience of writing code to solve problems and to model systems. Children become skilled at creating high quality products and content using digital technology. They learn how to be safe, responsible and critical users of technology.
The computing curriculum provides purposeful cross-curricular links with all subjects, as well as linking to learning outside of school, both at home and within the wider world.
Our ultimate goal is to draw together the strands of computer science, information technology and digital literacy, in order to equip children with the computational thinking skills and creativity they need to understand and change the world.
Implementation
We follow the Purple Mash scheme of work which covers the whole primary curriculum with a clear structure of progression building on children’s previous knowledge. Purple Mash uses resources embedded within the platform, which allow pupils to save, combine and import content, which can be shared across the school safely. In addition, we recognise the need to focus on developing vocabulary right from the start of the child’s journey. We endeavour to teach a wide variety of new vocabulary constantly in computing using foursquare activities, word walls and through general speaking and listening activities. The Purple Mash platform is also used across the curriculum to embed the use of technology in other subjects. The scheme is supplemented by additional lessons on computer networks and the use of BeeBots when creating computer programs.
We also participate actively in Internet Safety day, making good use of annual themes to raise the profile of different aspects of E Safety. In addition to the Purple Mash E Safety lessons, “Being Safe in a Digital World”, further learning takes place throughout the school year to maintain its profile. As a school, each class reviews the Internet Safety Agreement for their year groups and signs their agreement at the beginning of each academic year.

Art and design
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities in Art and Design. Our aim is to engage and equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding they require to be successful learners.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our Art and Design curriculum by developing a language rich curriculum by becoming ‘painting detectives’ to find clues, develop their visual literacy skills by making inferences and ‘read’ the stories that paintings tell.
It is mapped to include coverage of the national curriculum as well as numerous outdoor and collaborative learning opportunities and using the expertise of professional artists both in order to offer children chances to use a variety of techniques and materials that are valued and celebrated.
Our art curriculum challenges all pupils; engages their imagination by giving pupils the freedom of choice and the chance to explore and be creative across the curriculum. Art will encourage pupils’ curiosity by exposing them to rich and diverse works of art that develops a desire to want to discover more about our locality and the wider world and motivate them to take the next steps in their learning.
Our ultimate goal is for learners to see themselves as successful artists who enjoy being creative and having the confidence to take risks.
Implementation
At Carden, our design and technology curriculum is supported by the comprehensive scheme of work Projects on a Page developed by the Design and Technology Association to support primary teachers in delivering the national curriculum for design and technology in a manageable and inspiring way. It comprises 23 project planners covering a wide range of topics, including mechanisms, structures, textiles, food, and electrical systems, tailored for Years 1 through 6. The subject is taught by a specialist teacher who also has responsibility for art and design.
Each planner includes step-by-step guidance, teacher tips, glossaries, and examples of iterative design processes, all aimed at making planning and delivery straightforward and effective.
The scheme enables a strategic sequence of study that builds content and concepts over time, with skills and vocabulary comprehensively structured and sequenced across year groups with progression in knowledge. Where possible, units are matched and/or adapted to fit with topics making the learning more meaningful and relevant to pupils.
Impact
By the end of Y6, pupils will have the knowledge, understanding and skills in order to design and make high-quality prototypes and products for a wide range of users. They will have the ability to demonstrate creative, technical and practical expertise needed to perform everyday tasks confidently and to participate successfully in an increasingly technological world. Pupils will be able to critique, evaluate and test their ideas and products and the work of others. They will be able to apply the principles of a healthy and varied diet and be aware of a range of cooking techniques and understand seasonality and the origins of a variety of ingredients.

pageCache.pageTitle: English and Phonics – Carden Nursery and Primary School
pageCache.text:
English and Phonics
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities. Our aim is to engage and equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding to become lifelong readers, writers and communicators.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our language rich curriculum; talk being at the heart. We believe that strong oracy and writing skills are the keys for children to express themselves. Every unit of work is underpinned by talk: story-telling, role play, rehearsal – talk comes first. We believe that writerly skills should be explicitly modelled and practised, so children leave as confident writers.
Phonics is a powerful tool in learning to read and write, so this is a priority for our younger learners, alongside our Talk for Writing curriculum.
We believe that the curriculum is everything that happens throughout the day, both in and out of school; we value and celebrate experiences and achievements from home.
We strive to foster a passion and deep understanding of English as a means of communicating information; learning about the world and sharing stories. It is our intention to immerse pupils in the wonders of quality texts in order to instil a love for reading and a passion for discovery.
Our English curriculum challenges all pupils and engages their imagination, encourages their curiosity and motivates them to take the next steps in their learning. We aim to expose children to engaging and challenging texts which fully represent the whole community.
At Carden, we use the principles of Sounds Write to teach phonics and early reading. Sounds-Write is a structured, multi-sensory phonics program teaching reading and spelling through a systematic, code-oriented method, focusing on the connection between sounds (phonemes) and letters (graphemes). It builds foundational skills like blending (combining sounds) and segmenting (breaking words into sounds) through an incremental framework, starting with simple words and progressing to complex ones, teaching that sounds can have one-to-four-letter spellings and that spellings can represent different sounds.
The principle of speech-to-print teaches children to hear sounds in words and link them to letters. Essential core skills of blending, segmenting and phoneme manipulation are practised daily.
Sounds-Write is used from early years through to lower KS2. It is suitable for all learners, including those needing extra support, due to its structured and simple approach.
Letters are symbols for sounds.
Implementation
Our English curriculum follows the Talk for Writing and Reading approach. The Talk for Writing approach enables children to read and write independently for a variety of audiences and purposes within different subjects. A key feature is that children internalise the language structures needed to write through ‘talking the text’, as well as close reading. The approach moves from dependence towards independence, with the teacher using shared and guided teaching to develop the ability in children to read and write creatively and powerfully.
We underpin our English curriculum with an established core reading spine of quality fiction, poetry and non-fiction that all children experience and draw upon. Imaginative units of work are developed to create a whole-school plan that is refined over the years; is well-resourced and documented to release teachers from planning and preparation so that they can focus on adapting their teaching for children’s learning.
The key phases of the Talk for Writing process, enable children to imitate orally the language they need for a particular topic, before reading and analysing it, and then writing their own version.
The Talk for Writing approach has three main stages: Imitation, Innovation, and Invention. During Imitation, students internalise a model text through oral rehearsal and actions. In the Innovation stage, they adapt the model text with new ideas, working with the teacher. Finally, in the Invention stage, they write an original text independently, using the language and structure they have learned.
In September 2024, planning and teaching for Y6 pupils moved away from the pure approach of Talk for Writing as it was recognised that most were able to effectively write from the invention phase independently with some scaffolds for those needing support. This proved successful with end of year results above national average for expected and greater depth standard.
Talk for Reading is a comprehensive approach designed to cultivate critical, appreciative, and confident readers. It’s built upon a strong reading culture, effective teaching, and successful leadership, aiming to develop children into thoughtful and strategic readers who can learn from texts, discover information, and deepen their understanding of the world.
This program goes beyond surface-level comprehension, encouraging children to engage with texts critically, question what they read, and develop a love for literature. It fosters the habit of reading and thinking deeply, allowing young readers to participate in the reading conversation that spans centuries and connect with diverse ideas and experiences.
A key element of Talk for Reading is the daily teaching of vocabulary and knowledge across all subjects, recognising that a rich curriculum enhances comprehension. The approach utilises the gradual release of responsibility model, guiding children from dependence to independence through three phases:
Introduction Phase: Children gain a basic understanding of the text through repeated readings, initial responses, and vocabulary consideration.
Investigation phase: Students dig deep into the literary concepts that lie at the heart of the text’s core purpose, using strategic approaches and response activities (like drama or role-play) to build a strong connection with the material. This phase culminates in summarising and evaluating the main ideas.
Independent understanding phase: Children demonstrate their comprehension independently through discussion, in-depth questioning, applying learning to new texts, or creating their own writing in a similar style.
Impact
The impact on our children is that they have the knowledge and skills to be able to read and write successfully for a purpose and audience. As all aspects of English are an integral part of the curriculum, cross curricular writing standards will have also improved and skills taught in the English lesson are transferred into other subjects; this shows consolidation of skills and a deeper understanding of how and when to use specific language, grammar and punctuation.

Geography
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities. Our aim in geography is to understand the world around us by getting under the skin of people and places. We want children to build a bigger picture and discover where they fit. We strive to engage and equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding they require to be successful geographers. Learners will develop contextual knowledge of the location of globally significant places. They will learn to gather data and be able to identify physical and human characteristics through purposeful learning.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our language rich curriculum which is mapped to include coverage of the national curriculum as well as numerous enrichment activities and outdoor learning opportunities. Our geography curriculum challenges all pupils; engages their imagination to enable them to communicate what they have learnt in different ways. It also encourages their curiosity and motivates them to take the next steps in their learning.
We believe in giving children active, first hand experiences which provide them with an authentic route into the topic taught as well as facilitating a context for their learning.
Our ultimate goal is for all learners to be global citizens who are conscientious and are able to make informed choices and judgements relating to the world around them. We hope to inspire learners to make positive contributions within their community, respect diversity and value equality of opportunity both now and in the future.
Implementation
At Carden, we have worked to theme, group, and link geographic terms, locations and processes firmly with the topics and the scientific enquiries which the children are engaged in in each Year group’s programme of study. This is supported by detailed knowledge organisers and a progression of skills document for each year group.
Geography becomes the driver of at least one term in every year group, ensuring a high focus on its subject matter and development of its particular skills. It also ensures that the principles and the understanding gained from the study of geography are combined with those of maths, science, history and RE and that important cross curricular links are made.
Geography is comprised of several strands which each approach a different aspect of learning and encourage different skills and thinking processes:
Impact
Pupils develop their awareness of the world around them and the role they play within it. This includes their personal experience of different locations both locally, nationally and globally. This will enable them to develop a stronger understanding of the interrelationships between places, people, and processes. By developing these skills, our pupils will be able to better conceptualise geographical processes and the issues that they create in a wider context, and to see how our actions and those of people around the world have an impact upon people, places, and our planet beyond what we can see at a casual glance in our local area. As this awareness, understanding and skills grow, we expect pupils to develop an appreciation for our local environments; our global ecosystem and to have the skills necessary to identify and discuss issues. We want them to use their geographical understanding actively, to carry forward into the next stage of their learning and beyond.

History
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities. Our aim is to engage and equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding they require to be successful learners. Through exploratory learning of historical events, pupils are able to timeline the narrative of history and make links to the present. During in-depth study of historical events, pupils gain an understanding of the wider world and the consequences of choices past.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our language rich curriculum, which is mapped to include coverage of the national curriculum as well as numerous enrichment activities and outdoor learning opportunities. Utilising high quality resources and promoting both teacher and pupil talk, it ensures children can comfortably use a wide variety of historical terms to support their learning and understanding. Making use of local sites of interest, re-enactment and dress up days allows our pupils to see history through their own eyes and contextualise and solve problems as someone else in time. Our curriculum challenges all pupils; engages their imagination by being immersed in real-life experiences; encourages their curiosity and motivates them to take the next steps in their learning.
We believe that the curriculum is everything that happens throughout the day, both in and out of school; we value and celebrate experiences and achievements from home. By celebrating the commemorative and familial events relevant to our pupils and our wider community, we aim to help children understand the complexity of people’s lives, the process of change, the diversity of societies and relationships between different groups, as well as seeing, understanding and celebrating their own identity.
Our ultimate goal is for all learners to be successful, confident, happy individuals, who make positive contributions within their community, respect diversity and value equality of opportunity both now and in the future.
Implementation
At Carden, we have linked historic events, knowledge, skills and vocabulary through our Big 6 themes of democracy, invasion, invention, trade, exploration and empire. Pupils study each period of history through the lense of these themes which are woven through and underpin the curriculum. Detailed knowledge organisers and progression of skills documents support the learning at each stage.
Our history teaching and learning is fully diversified and significant work has been achieved in decolonising key aspects of the curriculum. We challenge Eurocentric perspectives by including diverse knowledge systems, histories, and voices, recognising how colonialism shaped what we learn. We have broadened the subject to reflect global contributions, acknowledging power imbalances, and creating more inclusive, representative learning environments for all students, rather than erasing existing knowledge.
Key aims of our history curriculum
Impact
Pupils will leave Carden with an increased critical and analytical thinking, making informed and balanced judgements based on their knowledge of the past; beginning to apply these to the issues they face in the present. They will have the knowledge and skills to challenge and question traditional narratives. Pupils will have developed their awareness and understanding of how historical events, including local history, have contributed and influenced societies around the globe to shape the modern world. Pupils will have a love of history and a desire to continue to explore in the next stage of their learning.

Maths
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities. Our aim is to engage and equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding they require to see themselves as mathematicians.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin our language rich curriculum which is mapped to include coverage of the national curriculum. We provide a consistent range of rich mathematical language throughout key stages to encourage learners to become confident in exploring and breaking down problems into simpler steps. Our maths curriculum, influenced by NCTEM, challenges all pupils; engages their imagination; encourages their curiosity and motivates them to take the next steps in their learning. This inspiration allows them to persevere in seeking solutions and reasoning the ‘why’ of their learning through making links and generalisations within mathematics.
We believe that the curriculum is everything that happens throughout the day, both in and out of school; we value and celebrate experiences and achievements from home.
Our ultimate goal is for all learners to be fluent in basic number facts to allow for active development through contexts. This will provide them with the opportunity to be successful, confident, happy individuals, who make positive contributions within their community, respect diversity and value equality of opportunity both now and in the future. Overall, these opportunities aim to give children a curiosity of maths that they can explore in everyday life and provide them with the skills necessary for the future.
Implementation
We are developing our approach to teaching for mastery. The principles that inform this approach can be found here. Our aim is for the maths curriculum to be taught in small coherent steps to ensure all children have enough time to learn and master key skills. Pupils are taught through whole class interactive lessons which include lots of opportunities for pupils to talk and discuss their ideas, to reason mathematically, to ask questions and to demonstrate their understanding. Stem sentences are used to support children to articulate their mathematical thinking and make generalisations. Planning incorporates the 7 steps to metacognition and pupils are encouraged to be active participants in their learning. Lessons provide the opportunity to review and consolidate previous learning as well as time for new learning. Children are taught to embrace the value of learning from mistakes and to persevere when faced with challenges.
We recognise that fluency with number facts is an important factor in enabling children’s success in mathematics. Learning key facts to automaticity helps to avoid cognitive overload in working memory and enables pupils to focus on new learning. Through the Mastering Number Programme in EYFS and Key Stage 1, children are taught about the composition of numbers using concrete, pictorial and abstract representations to develop their conceptual understanding of addition and subtractions facts. In KS2 children continue to practice accurate recall of facts and calculation procedures. They are supported to make connections and derive new facts from known facts.

Physical Education
Intent
It is our aim at Carden Nursery and Primary School to provide the opportunity for our pupils to safely experience a range of sporting activities for fun and enjoyment.
Through carefully planned PE and sports activities, we aim to ensure that all pupils are active, happy, healthy and enjoy Physical Education. We aim to encourage the love of sports through our purposeful PE program, developing pupils’ physical literacy thus providing them with a movement foundation and aiding lifelong participation in physical activity.
We help pupils develop a passion for a range of sports where they can use their imagination; develop physical skills and be curious learners – all the while encouraging them to develop their passion for sport outside of school in the local community. We strive to provide high quality PE and sports teaching in both curriculum and after school clubs providing pupils with extensive opportunities to learn outside.
We aim to ensure that within their own level of ability all learners can achieve and understand success though an active, language rich experience that enables them to reach their full potential. We value the benefits of PE and sport to help build children’s self-confidence, self-esteem and self-worth which is character building and essential for pupil development. We celebrate pupils’ physical success as well as their personal development in the ‘social me’, ‘thinking me’ and ‘healthy me’.
We value equality and aim to provide opportunities for all children to experience competition at a variety of levels including individually, inter-school and as part of a team through healthy competitive games held with other local schools.
Implementation
A highly experienced team teaches the PE curriculum. All areas of the national curriculum are planned and taught in a sequential manner, which enables pupils to practise and refine their skills during and across the years.
The curriculum is arranged so that the skills children develop first in each year group are fundamental to the acquisition of further skills, and are applicable to the widest range of sports and activities. Opportunities are built in through the year for dance and gymnastics, again sequencing the units so that the skills of agility, balance and coordination are constantly being revised and developed. This is supported by a skills progression document.
There is repetition year to year, with the same units falling into the same order across the vast majority of year groups. This cyclical approach allows children to revisit familiar skills and develop them, with each year becoming progressively harder. As the children move up through the school, there is also more emphasis on team competition and more opportunity for children to lead their own and each other’s learning. This consistency of approach allows children to revisit skills and develop them to the best of their potential.
Children are invited to attend competitive sporting events within the local area. This is an inclusive approach, which endeavours to encourage not only physical development but also mental well-being. These events also develop teamwork and leadership skills and are enjoyed by the children. Children’s achievements in and out of school are valued and celebrated on the weekly updates throughout the year. Whole school celebration and rewards encourage children’s participation in sport.
We regard swimming as being an essential part of the curriculum. Reception to Y3 children benefit from two terms of swimming a year in our onsite school pool. Pupils in Y4-Y6 continue their learning at a local high school pool. The swimming lessons provide children with the experience of water confidence and water safety, as well as learning stroke techniques. Carden has the highest number of pupils leaving a primary school within the city who can swim confidently.
Certain areas of curriculum teaching are supplemented by professional coaches such as tennis and football. We have strong links with Albion in the Community who support lunch time games and with Galaxy Girls who run our successful girls’ football team.
Residential experiences and adventurous outdoor activities are offered to pupils in Y4/Y5 with the Big School Camp. This is a two day/one night camping experience and activities on the school field. Y6 pupils take part in a three day/two night residential experience at YMCA Fairthorne Manor near Southampton.
Pupils are encouraged to further develop their PE interests further by taking part in one of our 22 sporting clubs that run at various times across year. We aim for all pupils to access at least one enrichment activity and have monitored this closely over recent years. Pupil voice has been an important part in this process; we have listened and actioned suggestions offered by pupils for different after school clubs.
Impact
PE is a strength at Carden Primary School. We are a Gold Mark Sports provision. All pupils learn that physical activity is important for their development, health and wellbeing and can be fun. We support all pupils to find a sport/physical activity that they enjoy and whilst traditional invasion games are an important part of the curriculum, we encourage pupils who prefer less active sports to find something that suits their needs and personality. We aspire for all pupils to see themselves as young sports people and hope to embed positive practices, attitudes and behaviours that they will carry forward into the next stage of their learning and adulthood.

Science
Intent
At Carden Nursery and Primary School we believe in providing high quality, active, purposeful and experiential learning opportunities in science. Our aim is to engage and equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding they require to be successful scientists. Our science lessons aim to encourage all pupils to think scientifically. We want pupils to ask key questions that lead to purposeful scientific investigations in order to develop their scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding of the world around them.
Our Core Values and Learning Journey Skills underpin the teaching of science by encouraging all pupils to be curious, active, adaptable and imaginative learners. Through our lessons, we aim to develop pupils’ science-specific language and vocabulary through enquiry, discussion and questioning.
Our science curriculum enables pupils to utilise various outdoor learning opportunities in and around the local area, ensuring links with the wider community where possible.
Science at Carden aims to challenge all pupils; engage their imagination through exploring, testing and reflecting on their own ideas. This encourages their curiosity and motivates them to take the next steps in their learning.
Science is regularly celebrated in lessons and throughout the school through awards, assemblies, displays, science focused weeks and parental/carer involvement.
Our ultimate goal is for all pupils to enjoy science and to view themselves as scientists. We want them to develop a passion for the subject so that they can carry their knowledge and understanding forward into the future and make important changes to the world.
Implementation
Planning for science is a process in which all teachers are involved to ensure that the school gives full coverage of, ‘The National Curriculum programmes of study for Science’ and, ‘Understanding of the World’ in the Early Years Foundation Stage.
Science teaching at Carden involves adapting and extending the curriculum to match all pupils’ needs to ensure they are challenged and achieve success, regardless of their starting point. Science can be linked to class topics where possible, or is taught as discrete units and lessons where needed to ensure coverage in line with the National Curriculum requirements. Teachers plan to suit their children’s interests, current events, their own teaching style, the use of any support staff and the resources available. Opportunities for enrichment are included during school trips; visitors to school and during National Science Week.
Scientific enquiry skills are embedded in each topic the children study and our curriculum is structured so that these topics are revisited and developed throughout their time at school. This allows the children to grow in their understanding, building upon their prior knowledge and increasing their enthusiasm for the topics whilst embedding this procedural knowledge into the long-term memory.
The physics aspects of the science curriculum is supported by The Ogden Trust which is UK-based charity dedicated to promoting physics education for 4-18 year olds, by boosting teacher confidence, providing free resources/CPD, and inspiring students to pursue physics, focusing on increasing post-16 uptake and ensuring access to quality, inspiring physics for all, particularly underrepresented groups.
At Carden, our Y6 science ambassadors champion the subject across the school and support younger children with their science lessons especially those that involve practical investigations and experiments.
Impact
The impact is to ensure pupils not only acquire the appropriate age-related knowledge linked to the science curriculum, but also skills which equip them to progress from their starting points, and within their everyday lives.
All pupils will have:
Our engagement with the local environment ensures that children learn through varied and first-hand experiences of the world around them. Children at our school enjoy science and this results in motivated learners with sound scientific understanding. Our pupils are learning that science in its many forms is vital to the world’s future prosperity and know and believe that they play a significant part in this future.

Carden hosts the Speech and Language Centre that supports pupils who have an education, health and care plan (EHCP) with a primary need of 'communication and interaction'. The school runs a 22-place centre which caters for children who have EHCPs with a primary need of ‘Communication and Interaction,’ with regard to speech, language and communication difficulties.
Places are allocated by the Local Authority in consultation with the school. Children are based in the Speech and Language Centre classrooms (EYFS/KS1 and KS2) and receive specialist teaching and therapy from highly trained staff.

Governors at Carden
Carden Primary School is thriving. This is an exciting school to be a governor; an inclusive school at the heart of a strong and diverse community. A recent monitoring visit by Ofsted, the schools’ inspector, confirmed that Carden Primary is still a good school. ‘Parents are very pleased with the school (and) appreciate the care and attention staff give to their children. Almost all those who completed Ofsted s survey, Parent View, would recommend the school.’
We are proud of our inclusive ethos, where everyone’s views are represented and everyone has a voice. We would like to encourage applicants from BAME or White other background or those who identify as disabled or LGBT to join the governing board to enhance the representation of these groups. We would also welcome parents who have a child with special educational needs. Diversity data is collected and analyzed by the board and, where possible, used in recruitment and training to ensure governors reflect the communities they serve. However this data not published due to reasons of confidentiality.
Being a school governor is a challenging but rewarding role. There is no requirement to understand the education system. Governors just need to have life skills, the time to share their experience, an enquiring mind and the confidence to ask questions. Above all, governors have to have a genuine interest in supporting the school and helping us to achieve the best outcomes for children. Excellent governor training, support and resources are provided.
If you have any questions or are interested in becoming a governor, please contact the Clerk: zoeheaton@carden.brighton-hove.sch.uk
What do governors do?
Governors are essential to the work of the school and are legally responsible for it. They are not, however, involved in the day to day running of the school which is managed by the Senior Leadership Team. This leaves governors free to focus on their core functions of:
Governors act as a sounding board for issues being reviewed within the school and work with the senior leaders to raise standards of achievement. They approve the school budget and appoint the Headteacher. They work as a team and make collective decisions, abiding by an agreed Code of Conduct .
As you would expect they need to gain an understanding of the school and its overall performance in order to explain its decisions and actions. This is done by attending regular meetings and carrying out school visits. They also attend training in order to keep up to date with the requirements of the role. More information about the role of governors can be found in the Governors’ Handbook.
Governing Body at Carden Primary School
Constitution
The governing body reconstituted in March 2015 and the number of governors on their Instrument of Government is now set at 12. This twelve is made up of different categories of governors. There are 7 Co-opted governors, 1 Headteacher staff governor, 1 staff governor, 1 Local Authority governor and 2 parent governors. The term of office for each governor (other than headteacher) is for four years, although being a voluntary position, governors may resign at any time.

pageCache.pageTitle: Special needs – Carden Nursery and Primary School
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs
Carden Primary School is a highly inclusive school where every child matters. Children at Carden Primary School enjoy a rich, diverse and stimulating curriculum, high quality teaching and excellent support for their individual needs.
We value the contribution that all children make and aim to support and inspire them all to learn and develop socially to the very best of their abilities. We encourage our children to develop as caring and responsible citizens, with a sense of belonging to our school community.
We make excellent provision for pupils’ individual needs and recognise their talents and abilities. The Speech & Language Centre which provides for children from across Brighton and Hove is a key part of our school. Skills and resources are shared between Centre and mainstream staff to support SEND pupils throughout the school and improve staff development and training at all levels.
Additional and/or different provision is currently being made in school for children with a range of needs, including:
Cognition and learning – mild and moderate learning difficulties; specific learning difficulties for example dyslexia and difficulties with maths; global developmental delay.
Communication and interaction – speech and language difficulties, including social communication difficulties and processing difficulties.
Social, emotional and mental health – attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, anxiety, attachment and social interaction difficulties.
Sensory, medical and physical – visual and hearing impairment, physical needs e.g. cerebral palsy, specific medical and genetic conditions.
Responsibility for the support of a child with SEND lies with the class teacher, supported by the Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCO). Some class teachers or year groups may work alongside a teaching assistant (TA) who supports all children in lessons, including, but not exclusively, those with identified SEND.
In some classes a TA may be allocated to a specific pupil and will support this pupil and other pupils in the class. The class teacher will implement strategies to support the needs of the children in their class through high quality teaching.
A small number of children may need additional support in order to help them to access their learning and the strategies will be tailor-made for each child’s needs. For example a child who has difficulties with reading may get daily reading with the TA, opportunities to practise their phonics and written instructions for tasks with added pictures (communicate in print).
A number of children will also be given withdrawal interventions and the school run a range of these through highly trained TAs. These interventions include School Start and Talk Boost speech and language programmes, Fisher Family Trust reading programme and First class at Number 1 and 2 maths programmes.
We also have four full time equivalent Learning Mentors who support children with social, emotional and mental health needs in order to help them to be emotionally and behaviourally ready to access their learning. These learning mentors support the school’s breakfast club.
The school also work with external professionals / agencies in order to gain support and strategies from professional colleagues. Many of these professionals now work as part of the Brighton and Hove Inclusion Support Service. These include specialist teachers in Speech and Language, Literacy, Sensory Needs and Autism Spectrum Condition as well as Educational Psychologists, Behaviour specialists and Primary Mental Health Workers.
The school also work with health professionals such as Health visitors, School Nurses, Speech and Language Therapists, Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists and many more.
Decisions over what provision a child may need will be made in the termly pupil progress reviews, half termly Achievement Teams as well as through discussion with the SENCO.

We believe a child cannot learn if they are not emotionally and socially nurtured. Strong relationships - between staff, pupils, and parents/carers - are the foundation for academic thriving and whole-child development for the real world.

Despite excellent results, we are continually improving our approach, and communicating with parents/carers in a number of ways, for example the Parent Representatives and the Parent-Teacher Association.
